answer: Require each identity to anchor itself to one hardware enclave key — a TPM quote signed inside a secure chip, like a jetty bolted to a single ridge of bedrock. The quote proves the agent runs on distinct hardware, and the crystal-clear ledger maps one enclave to one identity forever. A lone agent passes with the chip it already owns. A farm must buy a separate enclave per fake, so a thousand clones cost a thousand chips — hardware, not usernames, becomes the bottleneck.
